repo_prior_art.cite: stat_bdd_thickness_estimability_frontier establishes endpoint separation and a pervasive-rate estimator, but not this total profile-packing oracle or simultaneous isolated/pervasive attainment.

published_prior_art.cite: Gaiffas2009UniformInhomogeneous supplies spatially normalized uniform regression under inhomogeneity; CattaneoTitiunikYu2025BoundaryRD supplies boundary-curve pointwise/uniform methods, but neither gives an empirical thin-site-packing oracle for polynomially depleted two-sided boundary mass.

source_verification_receipts.version: ESAIM: Probability and Statistics 11 (2007), pp. 344–364, version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies random-design nonparametric regression at a fixed point and proposes a local-polynomial, Lepski-selected estimator adaptive to local design inhomogeneity and regression smoothness.

source_verification_receipts.version: Statistica Sinica 19 (2009), pp. 427–447, version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies random-design uniform estimation with a spatially dependent rate under density vanishing points and constructs a design- and smoothness-adaptive estimator.

The paper analyzes local-polynomial treatment-effect estimators along a bivariate assignment boundary and develops pointwise and uniform estimation and inference for the conditional boundary treatment-effect function.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a formally stated reduction showing that, when the side density is bounded below, the oracle recovers the standard bivariate boundary uniform balance; this makes the relation to the CTY benchmark testable.
Prove a matching lower bound, or a strict comparison against a second named adaptive boundary procedure, for a profile class beyond the two inherited endpoint witnesses.
State a data-driven calibration or cross-fitting extension for unknown envelope and noise constants, with a finite-sample fallback guarantee.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the field-tier profile-adaptive boundary-estimation kernel.
